clue.text: Expert attempt to decipher report

definitions.meaning: a ... shot or ... troops are expert, first-rate
to have a ... at something is to have a go, an attempt
to ... a code is to decipher it
a sharp report, like a gunshot

explanation.surface: A specialist is trying to decode a document.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions run together: adjective, noun, verb and noun, each a separate sense of the same five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Each clue word is a standard dictionary sense: skilled, a go, solve a code, a loud bang.

clue.text: Succeeded in puzzles containing challenge?

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: crosswords are puzzles
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
with can mean containing, as in a pie with apples

explanation.surface: Someone who did well at puzzles that contained a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra S sits between CROSS and WORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords with someone is to clash or argue with them, to take them on.

clue.text: Church agreed to hide bibles, oddly

indicators.note: to hide means to keep the following letters concealed within

parts.note: ay, a variant of aye, means yes, agreed

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A church consented to conceal Bibles, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a church belonging to a monastery or convent, like Westminster's.

clue.text: One believed in a shrink, originally

indicators.note: originally suggests the letters in a form other than the present one, here rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who trusted a psychiatrist at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One believed in' is a figure people believe in, a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Krishna is a Hindu deity, an incarnation of Vishnu, worshipped by believers.

clue.text: Aspire briefly to put an end to game

indicators.note: said briefly, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to aspire is to hope
to scotch a rumour or plan is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: An ambition, cut short, to stop playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is the children's playground pastime of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Attempt to attract attention with a kiss that deceives

parts.note: ho! is a cry to attract attention
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A deceptive try at catching someone's eye with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a trick or deception, something designed to fool.

clue.text: Wisdom of teacher, one capturing student's heart

parts.note: PROF is short for professor, a teacher

indicators.note: capturing means holding the following letter inside

parts.note: unity is oneness

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A teacher's wisdom captures a student's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Profundity is depth of insight or thought, deep learning.

clue.text: Discharge of guy arranged by stealth, finally

parts.note: cat is old slang for a man, a guy
arr. is the abbreviation for arranged by on a musical score

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

explanation.surface: A man let go after a stealthy plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like an anagram signal; with 'by' it is the music credit ARR.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is mucus discharged in the nose and throat during a cold.

clue.text: Play husband in new TV serial

indicators.note: in means the letter sits inside the rearranged letters
new means the letters are made into something different

explanation.surface: A husband appears in a new television serial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rivals is Richard Brinsley Sheridan's 18th-century comedy, source of Mrs Malaprop.

clue.text: Country's borders stand for the nominal length of this conflict

definitions.text: Country's borders stand for the nominal length of this conflict

parts.words: Country's borders stand for the nominal length of this conflict
parts.note: the edges of Country are C and Y; C stands for a hundred and Y for years, so they name the length of the Anglo-French war

explanation.surface: National frontiers encode how long a war lasted.
explanation.walkthrough: It is 'nominal' because the war lasted 116 years, from 1337 to 1453.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval Anglo-French conflict over the French throne, conventionally named for a century.

clue.text: Not to be left out, bio lab got involved

indicators.note: involved in the sense of tangled or convoluted, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone insists on being included as the biology lab became involved.
explanation.walkthrough: In music an obbligato part is one that must not be omitted, which is what the opening phrase describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian musical term meaning obligatory: an accompaniment part essential to the performance.

clue.text: Association football match, perhaps, at home

parts.note: a cup tie is a knockout football match, one example of a tie
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Football Association fixtures played on home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Association football' looks like one phrase; 'Association' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a link or connection, as in a book tied in with a film.

clue.text: On return after vacation, English Tory comes a cropper

indicators.note: on return, the collected letters are read from the end back to the start
words that have been vacated are emptied of their insides, leaving only their outer letters

explanation.surface: Returning from holiday, an English Conservative falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes a cropper' reads as an idiom for falling; 'comes' is wordplay and 'a cropper' the definition. EH, TY and CS, read backwards, give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a tool that crops grass or corn, hence something that crops.

clue.text: Stranger's endless challenge about to annoy one

definitions.note: stranger is, comparative adjective plus a contracted link

indicators.note: about means placed around the following letters
without its end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to query something is to challenge it
to irk is to annoy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An outsider's constant questioning is about to irritate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun, a newcomer; it is the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirky means odd or peculiar, so the comparative form means odder.

clue.text: The sound of this noisy performer hindered reply?

indicators.note: the sound of means what follows is said out loud

parts.note: a hindered reply is a clogged answer

explanation.surface: The noise from a loud entertainer stifled a response.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a British accent, 'clogged answer' runs into the performer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in wooden clogs stamps out rhythms, so the act is loud by design.

clue.text: Had yachtsmen on, did Carol?

definitions.meaning: a boat with sailors aboard ..., read as two words
to wassail is to go from house to house singing carols

explanation.surface: A boat with sailors aboard; did Carol come too?
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name; it is the verb, to sing carols.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing was festive carolling door to door, usually with drink involved.

clue.text: It holds in pants burst at seams

indicators.note: holds means wraps around the following letters

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess

explanation.surface: Trousers ripping at the seams, holding things in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers, fitting 'seams'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seams of coal or rock are layers, and substrata are underlying layers.

clue.text: Infused with energy, firm picked up

indicators.note: infused with means having something put into it

parts.note: firm means hard
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A company energised and acquired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like collected; here it means caught by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up news or a sound is to catch it with the ears.

clue.text: One might steal your job, or steal your Job?

parts.note: to steal is to rob
Job is a book of the Old Testament, abbreviated OT

explanation.surface: Warning about automation, then a jokey echo with the biblical Job.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital J turns job into the biblical book of Job, found in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Automated machines replace human workers, taking their employment from them.

clue.text: Stop pain

definitions.meaning: to switch something off is to stop it, as a verb phrase hyphenated here
a pain, someone off-putting or a nuisance

explanation.definitionFit: A turnoff is something off-putting, and to turn off is to stop or switch off.

clue.text: Oats we got free end in the bin?

indicators.note: set free, the letters are loosed into a new order

explanation.surface: Free oats we were given end up thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or effort that is wasted is metaphorically binned, thrown away unused.

clue.text: British statesman getting stick after defence cut

indicators.note: after places the stick behind the shortened defence
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a wall is a defence
a pole is a stick

explanation.surface: A British politician takes a beating after his defence fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Walpole is generally regarded as Britain's first Prime Minister.

clue.text: Skewered meat includes chopped tongue and a date

indicators.note: includes means holds the following inside

parts.note: satay is grilled meat on skewers

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Urdu is a language, a tongue

explanation.surface: A kebab with chopped tongue and a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a date' looks like the fruit; it is a day in the calendar, loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week can name a calendar day, as in meeting on Saturday.

clue.text: No fool in class at any time?

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: Was there never a dunce in the class?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no fool is bright and quick-witted.

clue.text: See you tidy, initially, then clean professionally!

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell, see you

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Goodbye, keep things neat, then have them cleaned by experts.
explanation.definitionFit: Car valeting is professional cleaning, inside and out.

clue.text: Tiny bit of black and blue material

definitions.meaning: blue means obscene, so this is porn

explanation.surface: A tiny speck of black on a blue cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A smut is a soot particle; smut is also obscene content.

clue.text: Last stage of the moon coming round weekly or monthly?

indicators.note: coming round means wrapping around the following letters

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter
a magazine, MAG for short, may be published weekly or monthly

explanation.surface: Lunar phases, weekly or monthly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weekly or monthly' looks like timing for the moon; it is a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, adult stage in an insect's metamorphosis.

clue.text: Possible description of wife, with clothes on: large

indicators.note: clothes means covers or dresses, so the punctuation mark wraps the next letters

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed straight after this word, a comma, is itself part of the wordplay
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A wife described as wearing clothes, and large.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation itself is wordplay: the mark after 'wife' is spelt out as a word, and 'clothes' has it wrap around the next two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A common-law wife lives with a man as his partner without a formal marriage.

clue.text: Democrat, if after backing, to visit US press baron — rashly perhaps

indicators.note: to visit means to go inside, so these letters sit within the press baron's name

parts.note: William Randolph Hearst was an American newspaper magnate

indicators.note: after places the reversed word behind the D
backing means the little word is turned round to read from the end

explanation.surface: A Democrat calling on Hearst, with the rider that he may be acting hastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the little word, which follows D; 'to visit' puts both inside the newspaper owner's name, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging in headlong, without forethought, is an example of acting impetuously.

clue.text: Key tenant's lost right at the start

indicators.note: lost means the letter is dropped from the word
at the start fixes the dropped letter as the opening one

parts.note: a tenant is a renter; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A tenant's key is missing, the right one, at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a door key; it is the computer keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Enter is the keyboard key that confirms input or starts a new line.
